label: May 18–24
title: “Be Strong and of a Good Courage” —  Joshua 1–8; 23

items.text: The Israelites faced the Jordan River, the walls of Jericho, and mighty peoples, all without Moses. Yet, the Lord declared, “Be strong and of a good courage.” This courage wasn't from their own strength, but because “the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.”

When we have our own rivers to cross and walls to bring down, wonderful things can happen in our lives. This is because the Lord promised, “the Lord will do wonders among [us].” Trust in His power to help you overcome your challenges.

As Joshua prepared to lead Israel into the promised land, the Lord encouraged him, “Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed.” This assurance was rooted in the divine promise that “the Lord thy God will be with thee whithersoever thou goest.”

The Lord gave counsel to Joshua about the scriptures, saying, “this book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night.” This diligent study of God's word would make his way prosperous and bring understanding.

When the Lord invites us to read the scriptures, He promises great blessings. By meditating on God's word day and night, we can experience prosperity and success in our endeavors, as promised in Joshua 1:8 and other scriptures.

Rahab's story in Joshua 2 demonstrates the power of both faith and works. Her faith in the Lord, coupled with her actions of hiding the spies and helping them escape, led to her salvation and the salvation of her family.

With faith in Jesus Christ, we can experience God’s “wonders.” Just as the Lord parted the Jordan River for the Israelites, He can work miracles in our lives when we approach Him with sincere faith and obedience.

The parting of the Jordan River was a powerful demonstration of God's power. It occurred only after the priests' feet were dipped in the water, signifying that obedience and taking the first step of faith are crucial to receiving divine help.

Obedience invites God’s power into our lives. As we learn from the battles of Jericho and Ai, facing temptation requires faith and adherence to God’s commandments. Disobedience, as seen in Joshua 7, can lead to spiritual defeat.

The name Joshua, meaning “Jehovah saves,” foreshadows Jesus Christ. Just as Joshua led Israel into the promised land, Jesus leads us to salvation. His mission is to save us and bring us into His eternal kingdom.
